message.content: {"caption":"A boxed “Main Agent Prompt” presents a staged workflow for programming tasks, followed by practical notes.","description":"A wide rectangular text panel with rounded corners has a dark teal header labeled “Main Agent Prompt” and a light gray body containing monospaced text. The body advises an experienced programmer to proceed in stages: slow down and avoid writing files fully end-to-end in one go; first understand the context by locating and reviewing useful project documentation, then examining relevant code to identify existing design patterns and conventions; optionally prototype with simple examples, compare approaches using execution feedback, and synthesize the findings into a design; make minimal effective code edits while following existing style; test end-to-end, preferring scripts without test frameworks unless that is unsuitable or a framework is already used, and check validity, regressions, and intended behavior; then update documentation and remove temporary files or changes. A “NOTE:” section says not to create virtual environments, to avoid pytest and mocks when possible in favor of end-to-end scripts, that clearly exploratory requests may bypass the rigorous procedure, and to call a reasoning agent for help with a tricky algorithmic or mathematical problem. The content is arranged as a numbered outline with indented substeps and dash bullets; there are no arrows, plotted data, or check/cross marks.","figure_type":"other","chart_values":[]}
